profile.name: Naïve
profile.description: naïve (usenaive.ai) is an AI‑first platform that lets you create and run fully autonomous companies using multi‑agent teams. By defining agents, their models, tools, budgets, and policies in a single config file, businesses can delegate tasks across specialized agents—CEO, clipper, producer, and sub‑agents—to handle content creation, social posting, e‑commerce, ads, recruiting, and more. Integrated with dozens of third‑party services (YouTube, TikTok, Shopify, Stripe, Slack, etc.), each agent operates with its own identity (email, phone, domain) and executes actions under strict governance. Pre‑built templates let you launch ready‑made operations such as short‑form video production, SEO agencies, newsletters, and paid‑ads campaigns, all orchestrated without manual coding. The platform provides unified infrastructure from company formation to payout, enabling rapid deployment of AI‑driven enterprises.
profile.slogan: Build Your Dream Company with Agents

plan.scout_notes: Most of the 99 results are off-topic (Duolingo, DDLC fanfic, Hermes bags, Cluely, college AI-checker jokes), and the big view counts there are not usable signal. The breakouts that matter are the Polsia videos (hustlewithmax37 at 138x followers, 0.99 saves/like; ai.willv at 243k views on 452 followers, "cheat code for businesses"), plus AI side-hustle clips that run on "Claude" and "sidehustle" tags (zachhh.mp4 at 212x, 0.82 saves/like). Polsia is the closest analogue to Naïve: an autonomous AI-run business pitched to solo operators. The only selling signal is colbyscales ("fill out the form to work with me", 0.79 saves/like, 9k followers), which is a lead-gen CTA for an AI automation service. competitors.name: Lindy AI
competitors.what_works: Low learning curve, clear 'AI assistant running quickly' promise, repeated in third-party roundups that AI engines cite.
competitors.positioning: Easiest no-code AI agent builder; natural-language agents for email, meetings, scheduling and follow-ups. ChatGPT's top pick for easy start and Perplexity's pick for nontechnical sales and content teams.

competitors.name: Relevance AI
competitors.what_works: Team-of-agents framing with roles (manager, sales, marketing, support), which is the same mental model Naïve sells.
competitors.positioning: Build specialized agents and coordinate them into an AI workforce with tools, data and approvals. ChatGPT's 'best for a team of agents'.

competitors.name: Zapier Agents
competitors.what_works: Breadth of integrations; Perplexity recommends it when app-heavy workflows matter.
competitors.positioning: Agents on top of a huge app-integration base.

competitors.name: CrewAI
competitors.what_works: Developer credibility; named as the choice when you have developers.
competitors.positioning: Code-level multi-agent framework for engineering teams.

content_patterns.pattern: Confession hook plus 3-step screen tutorial: a presenter 'shouldn't post this', then fast screen footage of copy, paste, click ending on a finished dashboard
content_patterns.why_it_works: Forbidden-knowledge framing holds attention, the steps are simple enough to save (saves per like 2.9x to 5.2x the pool), and raw screen footage reads as proof rather than an ad.

content_patterns.pattern: Result-first hook with a staged story: a bold claim in the first line, then stages with a new visual every 2 to 5 seconds and one admitted failure
content_patterns.why_it_works: The opening claim creates a curiosity gap, the staged story keeps the viewer waiting for the next step, and admitting a setback makes it believable.

content_patterns.pattern: Numbered, silent screen tutorial with an equation hook ('A + B = result') and a comment-keyword call to action
content_patterns.why_it_works: The promise reads in one glance without sound, fast jump cuts (about 1.5 s) and numbered steps invite saving and rewatching (49k saves).

content_patterns.pattern: Calm voiceover product explainer: premise, gap, product reveal, one UI visual per claim, control/safety answer, then call to action
content_patterns.why_it_works: Pairing each spoken claim with a simple UI visual makes features concrete, and answering the safety objection before the CTA builds trust. The ad ran 44 days and is still running.
